simple.meaning: אֲדֹנִיקָם (ʼĂdônîyqâm) is a Hebrew word meaning “Adonikam , the name of one or two Israelites.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֲדֹנִיקָם (H140) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 2:13, with occurrences in Ezra, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲדֹנִיקָם (H140) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֲדֹנִיקָם (H140) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֲדֹנִיקָם (ʼĂdônîyqâm) / H140 is traced through Ezra 2:13, Ezra 8:13, Nehemiah 7:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Adonikam , the name of one or two Israelites
definitions.full: H140. Adoniqam אֲדֹנִיקָם proper name, masculine ( my Lord has arisen ) head of a family Ezra 2:13 ; 8:13 ; Neh 7:18 ( אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ 10:17 ).
definitions.rootNote: from 113 and 6965 ; lord of rising (i.e. high);

occurrences.englishText: The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty-six.
Of the sons of Adonikam, who were the last; and these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah; and with them sixty males.
The children of Adonikam: six hundred sixty-seven.
